findings.explanation: Three interactive (UI-created) clusters have auto-termination disabled or set beyond the configured threshold of 60 minutes. Observed uptime materially exceeds observed activity, which is consistent with idle billing.
limitations: Idle percent is derived from cluster event timelines, not from per-second utilization.
A business requirement for always-on interactive compute would invalidate this candidate.
findings.recommendedAction: Confirm with each cluster owner whether an always-on interactive cluster is required. Where it is not, set auto-termination to the shortest interval that still meets the team's interactive workflow.
findings.title: Interactive clusters run without auto-termination

findings.explanation: Cost records representing 25.9 percent of in-scope spend cannot be attributed to an approved owner using the configured tag taxonomy. This exceeds the configured unattributed threshold of 5 percent.
limitations: Managed resource groups inherit tags from the parent workspace only when the workspace propagates them.
findings.recommendedAction: Run tag remediation with the resource owners named in the estate inventory, then re-run the assessment to confirm attribution coverage improves.
findings.title: A material share of spend carries no approved ownership tag

findings.explanation: Two job clusters place the driver node on spot capacity. Driver eviction terminates the entire run, so spot drivers trade a small unit-price reduction for a disproportionate reliability risk.
limitations: Observed eviction events are not available without cluster event retention across the full window.
findings.recommendedAction: Move the driver to on-demand capacity while leaving workers on spot, then confirm the job's failure rate over a full schedule cycle.
findings.title: Job cluster drivers are provisioned on spot instances

evidenceGaps.impact: No deep-dive job run IDs or table names were supplied, so stage-level Spark analysis was not attempted. This is an expected default, not a failure.

## 15. 30/60/90 roadmap

### Days 0-30: validate evidence and ownership

- **Confirm ownership for unattributed spend** (FinOps lead) — Work through the 25.9 percent of spend with no approved owner tag and assign an accountable owner per resource group.
- **Validate interactive cluster business need** (Platform engineering) — Interview the three interactive cluster owners and record whether always-on operation is a business requirement.

### Days 31-60: controlled validation

- **Pilot auto-termination in non-production** (Platform engineering) — Apply the agreed auto-termination interval in the non-production workspace and observe a full week of interactive usage.
- **Move job drivers off spot capacity** (Data engineering) — Set first_on_demand so the driver uses on-demand capacity and observe the failure rate across a full schedule cycle.

### Days 61-90: scale or stop

- **Scale accepted changes to production** (Platform engineering) — Promote only the changes that passed non-production validation, one workload at a time, with rollback criteria agreed in advance.
- **Establish budgets and alerting** (FinOps lead) — Create budgets for every active cost scope and route alerts to the accountable owner recorded in day 0-30.
- **Re-run the assessment and compare to baseline** (FinOps lead) — Re-run against the same window shape and compare against the recorded benefits baseline. Realized savings stay null until measured.
